data.description:
## What happens

When `gerrit_safe_submit.py` receives HTTP 409 from the revision-scoped submit
endpoint, it reports the refusal without the response body Gerrit returned. The body
carries the reason — a merge conflict, an unsatisfied submit requirement, a
Rebase-If-Necessary failure, or a genuinely newer patch set — and those demand
different responses from the caller.

## Why it matters

409 is the one status where the correct next action is not inferable from the status
alone. Without the body the caller has to open the change in a browser to learn
whether to rebase, wait for a vote, or resolve a conflict. In an agent session that is
a dead end, because the body is the only place the distinction exists.

## Change

Include Gerrit's response body in the error output on any non-2xx submit response, not
only 409. Strip the `)]}'` prefix if present so the body reads as JSON, and keep the
existing status line so the output is a superset of today's.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] **AC1** On a stubbed 409 whose body carries a `message` field, the script's
      stderr contains that message text verbatim.
- [ ] **AC2** The stderr also still contains the HTTP status code, so the output is a
      superset of today's.
- [ ] **AC3** A body prefixed with `)]}'` is printed with that prefix removed.
- [ ] **AC4** A body that is not JSON is printed as-is rather than raising.
- [ ] **AC5** The exit code on 409 is unchanged from today's.
- [ ] **AC6** Unit tests cover AC1-AC5 against stubbed responses, with no network access.
- [ ] **AC7** `make verify` exits 0.

## Out of scope

The abbreviated-SHA guard defect in the same script, tracked separately. This change
must not alter which revisions the guard accepts.
data.title: gerrit_safe_submit.py drops Gerrit's response body on a failed submit
